basis_status: INFERRED from code at the walked commit and HEAD, not measured on the wire. The one read that would measure it: the walk's local netlog.tsv (laptop only, named in the walk record at its Local artifacts section) -- the query string of the two refused reporting URLs.
whose_basis: The PAGE is not at fault on the firm binding: it binds the reporting requests to the picked client's own firm, exactly as it binds holdings and the directory browse. So the premise that the page offers a client of one firm while sending a request bound to none does not hold at the walked commit. The refusal sits on the service side: the reporting-read function is built for ONE firm (reporting-read/locals.tf:35-36 'this single role would then need to become one role per firm'; :57-58 'Any other firm's request is refused as unmapped, never defaulted'), while the project's own text puts a Cottonwood account in scope: IRPT_DASHBD_PRD.md:118-122 (FWD-11: 'an Inflection account and a Cottonwood account each get the same ... as a 49 Financial account') and DSGN_IRPTV1_PRD.md:44-47 (FWD-1: 'real Cottonwood data'). Deciding line: org/missions/D9/IRPT/IRPT_DASHBD/prd/IRPT_DASHBD_PRD.md:118-122. DSGN_IRPTV1_PRD.md:309 ('the backend is taken as is') concerns the account-level Performance route structure and does not decide firm coverage.
whose_open_reading: Two readings of the SERVICE finding remain for the CTO to name; no line chooses between them: (a) a defect of the deployed reading route against FWD-11 and FWD-1 (a Cottonwood client is offered by the page and refused by a function that cannot take its firm); (b) an outcome not yet built, FWD-11 not yet realized for the reading route, single-firm by deliberate design until the Inflection and Cottonwood adapters publish. Either way it is not a PAGE act, and the SERVICE option's wording (should resolve the firm from the picked client) is not what was found: the page already resolved it; the service lacks the firm in its map.
what_would_establish_it: Only for the label between (a) and (b): the CTO's ruling on whether FWD-11's realized state includes the reading route; and, for the code claim, the netlog read named in basis_status.
opal_user_default_sees: A selector left at Global (All) (firm.ts:27, :30; index.tsx:105) does not by itself cause the refusal: under it the page binds each reporting read to the picked client's own firm. For a client of Cottonwood (a firm not in the reporting-read map) the user sees what the walk saw: the picker label YTD unavailable and the Performance tab sentence 'Performance is not available for this client yet. It becomes available once Opal Capital computes performance for this account.' (walk record, hop 6), because the manifest and summary are refused FIRM_BINDING and the per-account performance read is refused OBJECT_NOT_COVERED (P2's cell, ruled in msgs 4414 and 4417). A client of 49 Financial would pass served.py:1212 (49financial is the map's one key) and would be answered from the published platinum files, if they are published (INFERRED, see also_live_state). Choosing the Cottonwood firm in the selector instead of Global would send the same firm word (the single-firm scope's registry_tenant), so it would not be expected to change the result (INFERRED; the single-firm resolve response carries registry_tenant only when the wire supplies it, ResolvedScope.ts:38).
